standard.title: Method for Determination of Centre of Gravity of Agricultural Tractors (कृषि ट्रैक्टरों के गुरुत्व केंद्र के निर्धारण की पद्धति)
standard.sector: Food and Agriculture / Agricultural Tractors and Power Tillers

sectional_committee.name: Agricultural Tractors and Power Tillers Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard prescribes the testing methods, apparatus, and calculation formulas to determine the three-dimensional position (longitudinal, transverse, and vertical/height) of the centre of gravity of agricultural wheeled tractors.
standard.scope: This standard prescribes the testing methods, apparatus, and calculation formulas to determine the three-dimensional position (longitudinal, transverse, and vertical/height) of the centre of gravity of agricultural wheeled tractors.

version.current_version: First Edition, 1983 (Reaffirmed 2004, 2014, and periodically verified up to the current active status)

amendments.summary: No active Indian amendments have been issued on this reaffirmed copy (NIL on this copy). It incorporates the technical parameters of ISO 789-6:1982 / Amendment 1:1996.

certification.description: Voluntary/Mandatory under Central Government agricultural testing directives. While IS 10743 is a procedural test code rather than a consumer product, compliance with its testing protocols is legally required for commercial tractor homologation, central and state tractor testing stations (including the Central Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institute - CFMTTI), and is mandatory to obtain national subsidy approvals and roadworthiness certifications.
requirements: The tractor must be unladen, in normal running order, with tanks for fuel, coolant, and lubricants fully filled. Tyre inflation pressures must be adjusted to the manufacturer's recommended specifications for normal road work.

Determines the horizontal distance (x) of the center of gravity from the rear axle center line using the horizontal weighing method:
x = (R_f * L) / W
where R_f = front axle reaction weight on the weighbridge (horizontal), L = tractor wheelbase, and W = total tractor unladen weight.

Determines the lateral distance (y) of the center of gravity from the longitudinal median plane of the tractor:
y = [(W_l - W_r) * t] / (2 * W)
where W_l = left-wheel reaction weight, W_r = right-wheel reaction weight, and t = track width of the measured axle.

Determines the height of the center of gravity above the ground (h) using the suspension and ground reaction method. This requires tilting the tractor by lifting one axle (typically the front axle) and measuring the change in wheel reaction weights on the weighbridge.

Mandates that during the axle-lift tilting procedure, the tractor must be raised to an angle (theta) between 20° and 25° to the horizontal. If a 20° lift is impractical or unsafe, a smaller angle is permitted, but it must not be less than 15°.

The calculation of center of gravity height from the ground must incorporate and correct for the static loaded radius of the rear tires (the height of the rear axle center line from the horizontal ground surface, r_stat).

For specialized agricultural machinery (such as straddle tractors with raised chassis), when the ratio of the center of gravity height to the average minimum track width of the axles exceeds 0.90, the maximum design speed is restricted to 30 km/h.

Observed or calculated values of weights, lengths, angles, and coordinates must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained must match the specified values.
